audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] and full phases[] award Malphite levels 1-5, first item AND two-plus items, while the prose directly beneath says Kassadin out-pokes him from level 3, that his armour build is 'wasted defense', and that two items is 'your scaling fantasy realized'. The packet's levelChart says Skill/Skill/Kassadin x5.
audit.why: Three sources on one page, two answers, and a 55.81% win rate over 86 games. The mirror file audits/top/malphite__kassadin.json reached the same conclusion from Malphite's side — that Kassadin reclaims the lane outright at two items — so a chart handing Malphite the back half contradicts the opposing page as well as its own.
audit.corrected: Flipped stages 3, 4-5, first item and two-plus items from Malphite to Kassadin in both layers — 'Malphite' and 'Kassadin' are both eight characters, so the applier's band allows it. Levels 1-2 and Level 6 are blocked, see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every phase 'why' was generic Kassadin boilerplate — 'you are the worst champion in the game for ten minutes', 'the survival grind' — describing a lane Kassadin loses. This is a lane he wins from level 3.
audit.why: The boilerplate tells the player to concede a poke war he is heavily favoured in, purely because Kassadin usually concedes it. Malphite's build is armour and Kassadin's damage is entirely magic; there is nothing to survive.
audit.corrected: phases[0] through [6] and breakdown.early/mid rewritten to the real shape: an even level 1-2, then Kassadin's poke, then the scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Granite Shield's recharge condition appears nowhere. It absorbs up to 10% of his max health and comes back if he is not hit for a few seconds.
audit.why: That is the whole rhythm of the poke war: a Null Sphere that pops the shield and is followed by nothing is wasted mana, because it regenerates. The commit has to land inside the window the poke opened.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, content.early and Trading Rules as a two-step: pop it, then go before it returns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard is described throughout as a slow that Riftwalk must escape. Riot's text says it STEALS move speed — and Riftwalk is a teleport, so a movement-speed debuff does not shorten it at all.
audit.why: The page builds a plan around blinking out of a slow that never affected the blink in the first place. The real point is the reverse: the Q cannot set up his ult on you, because your escape is not a run.
audit.corrected: Stated in phases[4], whys[4], spikes[2].text, wants.you[1], content.mid and breakdown.mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ground Slam's damage is derived from Malphite's ARMOR and is dealt as magic. Neither layer says so.
audit.why: It is the one place his armour stacking is not wasted against Kassadin, and it is also the one part of his output that Void Stone and the Null Sphere shield both cut — the two facts belong together, and the page had neither.
audit.corrected: Added to phases[3], whys[3], content.early and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d offered 'the fifteen-second invitation' after a spent Unstoppable Force, and the cooldown block carried no numbers at all.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s. Fifteen seconds understates the window by an order of magnitude and would have a player rushing a commit he has a minute and a half to set up. Seismic Shard is a flat 8s and Ground Slam a flat 7s.
audit.corrected: All three cooldowns written in, at breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, content.late and All-In Windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late instructs the player to 'Q-silence the counterplay', and tradeGood/dosFull/dontsFull repeat 'repeat every six seconds'.
audit.why: Null Sphere has no silence — Riot's text is damage, a channel interrupt and a magic shield — and nothing in Kassadin's kit is on a six-second loop.
audit.corrected: Silence replaced with the shield; the six-second cadence replaced with the Granite Shield recharge window, which is the timer that actually governs a commit here.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization gave the generic 'Rod of Ages into Mercs or Sorcs' line with no reference to the fact that Malphite is buying the wrong resistance.
audit.why: Against a full-armour opponent with no magic resist, magic penetration converts directly into damage and bulk is close to worthless — this is the one lane where that is unambiguous.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to buy penetration rather than bulk.

edits.before: Malphite has almost nothing to fight you with in lane — he stacks armor, but every point of damage in your kit is magic, so his entire defensive build is wasted, and your Void Stone passive even shaves 15% off the rare magic damage he might carry. The only real danger early is his Q (Seismic Shard) slow into a W-empowered auto, which can chunk your paper-thin levels 1-2, so don't sit in Q range while you CS. Last-hit with Null Sphere, soak the poke, and know he can't actually commit to a kill on you this early without his ult.
edits.after: Malphite has almost nothing to fight you with in lane — he stacks armor, but every point of damage in your kit is magic, so his defensive build is wasted, and Void Stone shaves the magic he does pay back with Ground Slam. The only real danger early is Seismic Shard stealing your movespeed into a Thunderclap auto, which can chunk your paper-thin levels 1-2, so don't sit inside its 625 while you CS. Granite Shield is 10% of his max health and recharges out of combat — pop it with Null Sphere, then farm.

edits.before: By level 3 with Null Sphere ranked you out-poke him outright — his armor does nothing against magic, and Nether Blade refunds your mana on every champion-hit so you never run dry harassing him. At 6, Riftwalk answers his whole gameplan: blink out of his Q slow, dodge the windup on his R dash, and reposition the instant he commits. The lane only flips on you if he lands R while your Riftwalk is down, so keep your blink available and force the poke war a magic-resist-less Malphite simply can't win.
edits.after: By level 3 with Null Sphere ranked you out-poke him outright — his armor does nothing against magic, and Nether Blade restores mana on the hit so you never run dry harassing him. At 6, Riftwalk answers his whole gameplan: it is a teleport, so his movespeed steal cannot shorten it, and you reposition the instant he commits. The lane only flips if he lands Unstoppable Force while your blink is down, so keep it available and force the poke war a magic-resist-less Malphite cannot win.

edits.before: This is your scaling fantasy realized. With Riftwalk ramping and Rabadon's/Nashor's online, your Q-E-R burst shreds his armor-stacked body — armor is irrelevant against a fully magic kit, and his lack of magic resist means he melts. His one threat is the R unstoppable flank to lock you down, so keep Riftwalk charged to blink out of the dash and never get caught flat-footed at an objective. Respect that one engage and you blink onto his backline freely while he can't touch you.
edits.after: This is your scaling fantasy realized. With Riftwalk ramping to 2 seconds and Rabadon's/Nashor's online, your Q-E-R burst goes straight past his armor-stacked body, and his lack of magic resist means he melts. His one real threat is Unstoppable Force on a 100-second clock flanking in to lock you down, so keep the blink charged and never get caught flat-footed at an objective. Respect that one engage and you blink onto his backline freely, fight after fight.

edits.after: Your magic poke ignores his armor entirely and Void Stone cuts what Ground Slam pays back — you control both the farm and the harass outright.

notes: MIRROR: audits/top/malphite__kassadin.json already exists and I reused its findings rather than re-deriving them — Void Stone plus the Null Sphere shield blanking Malphite's entirely-magic output, Riftwalk at 5/3.5/2s, and Kassadin owning the lane from two items. My side states the same facts inverted and does not contradict it. STILL BLOCKED BY THE LENGTH BAND (the mirror hit the same wall): win[0], win[1] and phases[0].side, phases[1].side read 'Malphite' where the packet's levelChart says 'Skill', and win[4]/phases[4].side read 'Skill' where it says 'Kassadin'. 'Malphite' to 'Skill' is 8 chars to 5 and 'Skill' to 'Kassadin' is 5 to 8 — both blow the 10% band. The four middle-and-late rows I could flip, because 'Malphite' and 'Kassadin' are the same length; the remaining three need doing by hand, and until they are the chart reads Malphite/Malphite/Kassadin/Kassadin/Skill/Kassadin/Kassadin, which is still an improvement on Malphite owning two-plus items. ALSO UNRESOLVED: full.diff is 'EVEN' (4 chars) and cannot be moved to 'FAV' (3) inside the band, so I nudged diffRating from 5.5/10 to 4.5/10 instead — a 55.81% win rate over 86 games is a real edge, not a coin flip, but the diff label still understates it. UNVERIFIED, REMOVED: content.early asserted Void Stone is '15% magic reduction'; Riot's description gives no figure, so I kept the mechanic and dropped the number. FINALLY, champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json claims 'Malphite bypasses stacking resistances (Granite Shield)'. Granite Shield is a max-health SHIELD, not percent-health damage — the rule fired on the wrong flag. Not written into anything.
